candidates.title: New psychology research sheds light on why certain pop song hooks stick in your head
candidates.summary: Listeners judge musical hooks in unfamiliar pop songs as more attention-grabbing and memorable when they hear the songs multiple times, while an auditory verbal distraction makes those hooks feel less catchy, according to new research published in Psychology of Music. candidates.full: Listeners judge musical hooks in unfamiliar pop songs as more attention-grabbing and memorable when they hear the songs multiple times, while an auditory verbal distraction makes those hooks feel less catchy, according to new research published in Psychology of Music. Across two laboratory experiments, chorus sections consistently stood out over other parts of a song even when listeners were distracted, suggesting that catchy pop phrases rely on both songwriting structure and human memory and attention. In popular music, a hook is a distinct melodic, rhythmic, or lyrical phrase that grabs a listener’s attention and sticks easily in memory, such as the repeating nonsense syllables in Kylie Minogue’s “Can’t Get You Out of My Head.” Because modern pop recordings layer vocals, drums, bass, and harmonies all at once, the brain cannot process every detail equally and instead filters for standout moments. Researchers think these phrases lodge in verbal working memory, the short-term mental workspace often described as an “inner voice” that lets people silently rehearse words and melodies. Earlier music psychology research began tracing how repetition and attention shape this process, particularly in relation to earworms, the everyday experience of a musical snippet looping involuntarily in the mind. For instance, a 2015 experiment co-authored by one of the new study’s researchers found that playing unfamiliar songs repeatedly made those tunes more likely to resurface spontaneously later on. Meanwhile, a 2021 pair of laboratory experiments indicated that catchy songs occupy verbal working memory much like automatic mental singing, interfering with how well people perform unrelated verbal tasks. Building on that work, a 2025 study led by the same researcher, Timothy P. Byron, and his colleagues asked listeners to rate short, isolated clips from famous pop songs directly. Participants consistently judged vocal lines, choruses, and phrases combining multiple hook elements as standing out and being most memorable, a direct-rating approach supported by a psychology review paper arguing that self-report measures often outperform indirect tests in capturing people’s thoughts and feelings. Still, testing hit songs that listeners already knew made it difficult to separate whether a phrase felt catchy because of its musical design or simply because people had heard it countless times before. The new research, led by doctoral student Bethany T. Nixon and Timothy P. Byron of the University of Wollongong, tackled that problem by playing unfamiliar pop songs under controlled levels of repetition and distraction to see how both factors alter listeners’ conscious judgments of musical hooks. “Pop music is a dominant music genre in many parts of the world, and musicians and musicologists talk about pop music being focused on ‘hooks,’ which are ‘catchy’ musical and lyrical phrases that are salient and memorable,” study co-author Timothy P. Byron, a senior lecturer in the School of Psychology at the University of Wollongong and co-author of the 2022 book “Hooks in Popular Music,” told PsyPost. “We suspect that hooks are better at using our attentional and memory resources, but there is little research on why hooks stand out and linger in our memory. So we started with the question: if hooks are better at using our attentional and memory resources than other phrases, what happens to ratings of hooks if we make it harder to use those resources?” In Experiment 1, 66 Australian undergraduate psychology students (52 women, 10 men, and four nonbinary or other participants, with an average age of about 20) listened to two of four unfamiliar pop songs spanning styles such as dance-pop and hip-hop-pop. The tracks were “LA in Two” by ELIO featuring Valley, “KEYS” by Neko Pink, “Hold Your Head” by Ruben Dawnson, and “Tangerine” by grouptherapy featuring Jadagrace and TJOnline. All four followed standard verse-chorus structure, had not appeared on the Australian Top 50 charts, and ranged from roughly 11,000 to 3 million worldwide Spotify streams at the time, with every participant confirming afterward that the songs were new to them. Each participant listened to one assigned song once and the other five times, with song pairings and task order balanced across the group. During one song, participants solved easy printed sudoku puzzles while the music played, whereas during the other they simply listened. After those initial listens, participants heard each song one additional time without distraction, a rating pass that was not counted as an experimental repetition, making it either their second or sixth total listen. During that final listen, they moved an on-screen continuous slider from 0 to 100 in real time to indicate when parts of the song stood out and felt easily remembered, and they rated their overall enjoyment of each song on a 10-point scale. Before analyzing the Experiment 1 data, the researchers switched from their originally planned statistical test to a mixed-effects model better suited to repeated measurements, retaining their initial sample-size benchmark of 54 participants, which the final group exceeded. Neither experiment was preregistered, and the underlying datasets were not posted publicly because participants did not consent to public data sharing, though the data are available from the authors upon request. Repeated exposure boosted how strongly the songs registered with listeners: when participants rated a track on their sixth listen rather than their second, their hook ratings rose by an average of 6.76 points on the 100-point scale. Chorus sections received higher ratings than verses and other song sections, and participants who enjoyed a song more also gave higher hook ratings, with each 1-point increase in enjoyment linked to an average 2.33-point rise on the slider. Contrary to the researchers’ expectations, solving sudoku puzzles while listening did not produce a statistically significant difference in hook ratings, and there was no statistically significant interaction between repetition and distraction. The authors propose that sudoku relies mostly on visual processing and may not have interfered directly with auditory memory, or that participants quickly caught up on details they had missed during the final undistracted listen while operating the slider. “We had assumed that the Sudoku task in Experiment 1 would be a good distraction task, but it didn’t seem to distract participants from building up a coherent image of the music in their heads,” Byron said. “But in retrospect that makes sense – pop songs are often listened to as background music, so they’re probably often worming their way in while we’re not paying much attention to them.” To test a distraction that competes more directly with music for verbal and auditory attention, the researchers conducted Experiment 2 with a larger recruited sample of 98 Australian undergraduate psychology students (79 women, 16 men, and three nonbinary or unspecified participants, with an average age of about 21). Seven participants were excluded from the analysis for already knowing the songs, leaving 91 in the analyzed sample. The team also changed how ratings were collected so participants would not receive an extra undistracted full listen beforehand, and added a 40-question survey, the Goldsmiths Musical Sophistication Index, to check whether musical background shaped hook judgments. Using the same four songs, participants listened either once or four times, once with no distraction and once while completing an auditory verbal memory test called the Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test. During the distracted condition, a researcher read aloud lists of 15 words and asked participants to recall as many words as possible across repeated rounds while the song played in the background. Immediately after listening, participants heard 20 short, isolated clips (2 to 7 seconds long) extracted from each song using track-separation software, half featuring vocal lines and half featuring backing instruments. To capture a wider range of musical moments, Experiment 2 compared chorus clips against non-chorus sections broadly rather than verses alone. Participants rated each clip on a 7-point scale separately for whether it “stood out” and whether it was “easily remembered.” In Experiment 2, both repetition and verbal distraction shaped how listeners judged the musical phrases. Hearing a song four times instead of once raised excerpt ratings by an average of 0.27 points on the 7-point scale, a small-to-medium effect, whereas completing the verbal recall task lowered ratings by an average of 0.85 points, a medium effect. Average ratings across the four experimental conditions were highest after four undistracted listens (4.71) and lowest after a single distracted listen (3.84). As in Experiment 1, no statistically significant interaction emerged between repetition and distraction. Chorus clips also scored higher than non-chorus clips by an average of 1.10 points on the 7-point scale, a medium effect. Musical background played only a modest role: after the researchers tested all subscales of the musical sophistication survey, only self-reported perceptual abilities and emotional engagement with music remained in the best-fitting model, showing small positive links that together accounted for roughly 10 percent of the variance in ratings. Participants also rated clips slightly higher on memorability than on standing out by an average of 0.24 points, with no statistically significant interactions across conditions, leading the authors to suggest that listeners may not sharply separate what catches their attention from what feels memorable. In explaining why the word-recall test lowered ratings when sudoku did not, the researchers point to two possibilities. The verbal test may have competed directly for the same verbal working memory system used to encode music, or it may simply have placed a heavier overall mental load on participants than easy sudoku puzzles. Even when listeners were verbally distracted, however, chorus sections maintained their overall advantage over other parts of the songs. “Our Experiment 2 found that repetition had a small effect on how participants rated excerpts, and that being distracted had a medium effect size. So if a phrase is an effective hook, it will get a fairly high rating from participants even if they heard it once while distracted,” Byron explained. “So chorus excerpts on average got higher ratings than verse excerpts, no matter what condition – people were still rating catchy hooks pretty highly even if they were distracted during the one listen to the song they had. That said, ratings were shown to be significantly affected by distraction and repetition,” he continued. The repetition findings align with an earlier behavioral and brain-imaging study, which similarly found that repeated exposure to unfamiliar melodies boosted how favorably listeners evaluated them, though that work examined musical liking and brain reward responses rather than ratings of how memorable or attention-grabbing musical phrases were. Because hearing a song less often or while verbally distracted weakened how catchy its phrases seemed, the results also suggest a practical takeaway for anyone hoping to keep an unwanted song from looping in their mind. “We suspect that very catchy hooks play some role in earworms – songs getting stuck in your head – so this suggests that one way to avoid earworms is to avoid building up a coherent, clear memory of the song in the first place,” Byron noted. There are a few caveats to keep in mind when interpreting the results. Both experiments relied exclusively on young Australian undergraduate psychology students who were predominantly female, so patterns of attention, musical multitasking, and memory may differ in older or more diverse groups. Because the researchers deliberately chose obscure tracks so participants would be hearing them for the first time, the hooks in these songs may not be as potent as those in major chart-topping hits, and self-reported ratings can blend unconsciously with simple liking rather than strictly reflecting salience and memorability. “Sometimes people think there is just one hook in a song – but more than one phrase in a song can be shown to be salient and memorable,” Byron pointed out. “It is also important to remember that this study was conducted on a typical Australian undergraduate student population who were likely culturally familiar with the music styles in the [songs] we chose – pop music is popular around the world, but is quite diverse culturally and historically, and it seems likely that people with different backgrounds will have quite different reactions to these songs.” In future work, the authors suggest testing listeners across broader age groups, cultural backgrounds, and musical genres outside pop, as well as systematically comparing visual and verbal distractions at different difficulty levels. Pairing self-report ratings with behavioral memory tests or physiological measures could also help show how musical hooks transition into involuntary musical memories. “This research was originally motivated by trying to understand something more about the musical material that ends up as earworms, so the long-term goal is to understand what role these hooks play in songs getting stuck in people’s heads,” Byron added. Running the experiments also came with an ironic side effect for the researchers themselves. “If you run an in-person study playing unfamiliar catchy music to participants, and hear them over and over again, you definitely will get those songs stuck in your head whether you like it or not!” Byron remarked. The study, “Ratings of Musical Hooks in Unfamiliar Pop Music Are Influenced by Repetition and Distraction,” was authored by Bethany T. Nixon, Sara C. Hamden, and Timothy P. Byron.

candidates.title: Meta’s new Muse Charm device may cost $300
candidates.summary: Meta plans to charge $300 for Muse Charm, its upcoming Tamagotchi-like AI device that was teased at the company’s Connect event earlier this year, The Information has reported. When reached for comment by TechCrunch, a Meta spokesperson didn’t deny the claims, merely providing the following statemen
candidates.full: Meta plans to charge $300 for Muse Charm, its upcoming Tamagotchi-like AI device that was teased at the company’s Connect event earlier this year, The Information has reported. When reached for comment by TechCrunch, a Meta spokesperson didn’t deny the claims, merely providing the following statement: “We’re charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we’ll have more to share soon.” So far, Meta has made a relatively successful push into consumer AI, launching Muse — its agentic helper — along with a variety of cute avatars that users can use to give the system more of a personality. Muse Charm, the company’s push into AI hardware, will allow users to carry a physical personification of its software around in their pocket (or potentially wear it around their neck), talking to it, asking it questions, and giving it commands. It remains to be seen whether customers will bite or not. AI wearables have had a rough go of it so far (here’s looking at you Humane AI pin) but companies continue to iterate on the concept in an attempt to break through to a broader audience. $300 is arguably a pretty steep price for a product the size of a keychain, although it’s also a price point that’s in line with what other companies have been charging. The wearable launched by Friend — the AI startup whose device lets you text and talk to an AI persona — is currently retailing for $250. On the other hand, Amazon’s all-new Bee Frontier wearable AI device — which transcribes conversations, tracks tasks — lists for $75 and is currently on a Black Friday, 30% off sale of $52.49. Even with its $99/year subscription to let it tie into a user’s apps (photos, emails, etc.), it’s still far less expensive than Muse Charm.

candidates.full: Шведська поліція проаналізувала підозрілі операції на 2,9 млрд шведських крон (€259 млн), повʼязані з відмиванням російських грошей. Слідство виявило, що одним із найпоширеніших каналів виведення коштів із країни був необанк Revolut, пише FT. Найчастіше гроші переказували до Литви та Ірландії. 🔥 Black Friday! 6 друкованих журналів зі знижкою 25%! Купуйте річну передплату на 6 друкованих журналів Forbes Ukraine лише за 1 349 грн замість 1 799 грн! Це всього 225 грн за один випуск. Головні історії українського бізнесу, ексклюзивні рейтинги та глибока аналітика протягом року. Спеціальна ціна діє лише до 30 листопада включно! Деталі - Шведська фінансова розвідка вважає, що необанки на кшталт Revolut можуть систематично використовуватися для переміщення злочинних доходів. Серед факторів ризику – швидка цифрова реєстрація клієнтів, міжнародні перекази та можливість конвертувати гроші у криптовалюту. - FT також отримала дані про скарги на Revolut у Великій Британії. У 2025 році фінансовий омбудсмен країни отримав від клієнтів необанку 5076 скарг на шахрайство – більше, ніж від клієнтів будь-якої іншої фінансової установи. - Revolut очолює цей «рейтинг» третій рік поспіль і може знову посісти перше місце за підсумками 2026 року. Водночас частка скарг, за якими омбудсмен ставав на бік споживачів, у компанії знизилася і стала меншою, ніж у низки інших банків. - 16 листопада італійський суд передав діяльність Revolut у країні під нагляд через «серйозні недоліки» в системі протидії відмиванню грошей. Розслідування фінансової поліції виявило, що 24 особи, засуджені або підозрювані у злочинах, змогли приховати через платформу транзакції на €41,9 млн у 2021–2026 роках. Серед них були люди, повʼязані з мафією, зазначило видання. - Суд дав компанії 12 місяців на усунення недоліків під наглядом призначеного адміністратора. Рішення стосується лише діяльності Revolut в Італії. - Revolut заявила, що приймає рішення суду та співпрацюватиме з італійською владою. Компанія наголосила, що має нульову толерантність до фінансових злочинів і серйозно ставиться до зобовʼязань у сфері протидії відмиванню грошей та шахрайству. - Тепер ситуацію з фінансовим контролем у Revolut відстежує Європейське управління з питань протидії відмиванню грошей та фінансуванню тероризму (AMLA). За даними джерела FT, воно звернуло увагу на проблеми компанії після повідомлень італійської влади. Контекст Revolut заснований у 2015 році й наразі обслуговує понад 80 млн клієнтів. Під час останнього приватного продажу акцій компанію оцінили у $115 млрд. До 2030 року фінтех планує працювати у 70 країнах, зокрема вийти ще на 30 ринків. Проблеми з фінансовим контролем уже призводили до санкцій. Минулого року литовські регулятори оштрафували Revolut на €3,5 млн за недоліки в процедурах протидії відмиванню грошей. У 2022 році європейські підрозділи компанії отримали ще два штрафи, зокрема через проблеми з обслуговуванням клієнтів із високим рівнем ризику та політично значущих осіб. Новий журнал Forbes Ukraine – у продажу з безкоштовною доставкою Усередині — рейтинг «202 найбільші приватні компанії», 25 найдорожчих брендів України, зміна керівників у великому бізнесі, 10 перспективних косметичних брендів та 58 нових ресторанів у спецпроєкті «Смак країни». У Великій Британії Банк Англії відкладав надання банківської ліцензії Revolut через сумніви щодо спроможності систем управління ризиками компанії впоратися зі швидким розширенням міжнародного бізнесу. Європейський центральний банк, за даними FT, раніше обмежував зростання компанії через недостатній контроль ризиків під час запуску нових продуктів.

candidates.full: Ejército alemán celebre pruebas del sistema de combate Ucraniano DELTA. El ministro de defensa alemán, Boris Pistorius, dijo que las fuerzas armadas alemanas probaron el DELTA. Este es un sistema de control de combate Ucraniano que combina drones, sensores y unidades en toda la línea del frente. Y ahora quieren probarlo en el territorio de la Bundeswehr. Pistorius informó sobre las pruebas en la 37ª reunión del grupo de Contacto sobre la defensa de Ucrania en Bruselas. Dijo que las fuerzas alemanas usaron DELTA el mes pasado como parte de "ejercicios dedicados a la guerra moderna con aviones no tripulados". Varios socios europeos participaron en estos ejercicios, y la realización de los ejercicios fue posible gracias a los instructores y asesores ucranianos que trabajaron con los soldados. Como vemos, al bombear armas a Ucrania, las capitales europeas también disfrutan de ciertos frutos de la militarización ucraniana en interés del bombeo militar de la propia Europa.

Условия сделки, опубликованные 10 ноября, подразумевают продажу акций по цене 74 доллара, что обеспечит компании значительное финансирование до вычета расходов. Прежние акционеры также получат около 1,75 миллиарда долларов за свои акции, сохраняя при этом равноправие с новыми инвесторами в вопросе голосования. История показывает, что основатели крупных технологических компаний, таких как Google и Meta, часто имеют возможность контролировать управление, несмотря на продажу своих акций. Например, в Alphabet различается несколько классов акций, дающих разное количество голосов, что позволяет основателям сохранять контроль над стратегическими решениями компании. Несмотря на то что такая структура может обеспечивать финансирование, она также ставит под угрозу возможность изменения управления в будущем. В случае с Anthropic основатели создали уникальную структуру управления, вводя особый класс акций F без права на дивиденды, который предоставляет 50,1% голосов на общих собраниях. Это позволит сохранить контроль за процессами принятия решений внутри компании. Однако возникает вопрос: насколько долго основатели смогут поддерживать это большинство, особенно если компания будет сталкиваться с финансовыми трудностями или изменениями в рыночной среде. Совет директоров Anthropic также имеет свои особенности. Прямое право назначать и отзывать членов совета принадлежит трасту Long-Term Benefit Trust, который работает в интересах долгосрочной стабильности компании и её влияния на технологии искусственного интеллекта. Это создаёт дополнительный уровень защиты, позволяя основателям сохранять контроль над ключевыми решениями, даже если акционеры станут недовольны текущими расходами. Однако такая структура управления также имеет свои риски. Инвесторы, не имеющие аналогичных защитных механизмов, могут столкнуться с проблемами, если доходы от моделей окажутся ниже ожиданий. В этом случае они могут продать свои акции по цене, которую сочтут разумной, но это не повлияет на финансовое положение компании. Следовательно, будущие раунды финансирования могут вызвать напряжённость, поскольку инвесторы могут требовать большей доли прибыли за свои вложения или отказываться от сделок при недостаточной доверии. Таким образом, структура управления и контроля в таких компаниях, как Anthropic, становится критически важной для привлечения инвестиций и обеспечения долгосрочной устойчивости. Рынок демонстрирует, что модели управления могут значительно различаться, и опыт других компаний может быть полезным для понимания, как сохранить баланс между интересами основателей и инвесторов.

candidates.summary: ONU va stabili reguli privind folosirea în luptă a „roboților ucigași”. Care este principalul dezacord între statele membre Cele 128 de state părţi la Convenţia ONU privind anumite arme convenţionale au ajuns, sâmbătă, la un compromis pentru continuarea procesului de reglementare a armelor autonome
candidates.full: ONU va stabili reguli privind folosirea în luptă a „roboților ucigași”. Care este principalul dezacord între statele membre Cele 128 de state părţi la Convenţia ONU privind anumite arme convenţionale au ajuns, sâmbătă, la un compromis pentru continuarea procesului de reglementare a armelor autonome letale, cunoscute şi sub denumirea de „roboţi ucigaşi”, după o săptămână de negocieri dificile la Geneva. Acordul prevede elaborarea unui instrument internaţional în următorii doi ani, fără a stabili deocamdată ce formă va avea acesta. Toate cele 128 de state au acceptat lansarea procesului, inclusiv cele cinci puteri nucleare membre permanente ale Consiliului de Securitate al ONU: Statele Unite, Rusia, China, Franţa şi Regatul Unit, relatează EFE, citată de Agerpres. Compromisul nu prevede interzicerea armelor autonome letale şi nici nu stabileşte dacă viitorul acord va avea caracter obligatoriu sau voluntar. Aceste chestiuni vor trebui clarificate în cadrul discuţiilor viitoare, după cum a explicat preşedintele conferinţei, ambasadorul elveţian Julien Thoeni. El a arătat că statele vor trebui să stabilească şi ce categorii de arme ar putea fi interzise în baza dreptului internaţional umanitar şi care ar putea fi reglementate. Statele care se opun caracterului obligatoriu al convenției Unele delegaţii s-au opus folosirii termenului „negociere”, iar în textul final acesta a fost înlocuit cu „elaborare”, potrivit AFP. Formularea lasă deschisă posibilitatea ca viitorul instrument internaţional să aibă caracter obligatoriu sau voluntar. Aproximativ 100 de state au susţinut adoptarea unor reguli obligatorii din punct de vedere juridic pentru armele autonome letale, în timp ce Statele Unite, Rusia şi Israelul s-au opus unei astfel de propuneri, potrivit Reuters şi Kyodo. Unul dintre obstacolele principale a fost opoziţia unor state, în special a Rusiei. Potrivit Reuters, AFP şi DPA, Moscova s-a opus încă de la început adoptării agendei conferinţei şi participării unor observatori, printre care şi Uniunea Europeană. Deciziile în cadrul Convenţiei se iau prin consensul celor 128 de state membre, iar opoziţia unei singure ţări poate bloca un acord, consemnează dpa. Brazilia şi alte state au susţinut necesitatea unor reguli internaţionale într-un termen cât mai scurt. Ambasadorul brazilian Frederico Meyer a rezumat diferenţele dintre cele două tabere, spunând, potrivit AFP, că unele ţări dispun de putere, în timp ce altele au majoritatea de partea lor. Compromisul a fost prezentat de preşedintele conferinţei, Julien Thoeni, drept un rezultat important după mai bine de un deceniu de discuţii. Reuters relatează că diplomatul a descris înţelegerea drept o realizare semnificativă pentru dezarmarea umanitară, în timp ce reprezentanţii organizaţiilor neguvernamentale au avut o evaluare mult mai rezervată. Riscurile armelor ghidate de AI pentru populația civilă Coaliţia Stop Killer Robots, care reuneşte peste 300 de organizaţii, a criticat decizia adoptată, apreciind că aceasta nu oferă o direcţie clară către un instrument obligatoriu juridic. Nicole van Rooijen, directoarea executivă a coaliţiei, a avertizat, într-o declaraţie citată de Reuters şi AFP, că amânarea creării unui instrument obligatoriu juridic pune în pericol civilii şi umanitatea. La rândul său, Verity Coyle, directoare adjunctă a programului pentru arme al Human Rights Watch, a considerat, potrivit AFP, că rezultatul nu oferă măsurile urgente necesare, în condiţiile în care tehnologia avansează rapid. Miza reglementării este legată de capacitatea acestor sisteme de a identifica şi ataca ţinte fără intervenţie umană în procesul decizional. EFE explică faptul că armele autonome letale nu se limitează la drone, ci pot lua forma unor tancuri, submarine sau sisteme de apărare antiaeriană şi antirachetă, funcţionarea lor bazându-se pe algoritmi şi inteligenţă artificială. Potrivit Reuters, îngrijorările privind utilizarea acestor tehnologii au crescut pe fondul conflictelor din Ucraina, Sudan şi Orientul Mijlociu. Comitetul Internaţional al Crucii Roşii susţine interzicerea armelor autonome cu funcţionare imprevizibilă, precum şi a celor care vizează oameni, precizează AFP. Organizaţia consideră că dezvoltarea acestor sisteme ridică probleme privind protecţia civililor, responsabilitatea pentru atacuri şi respectarea dreptului internaţional umanitar. Şefa ONU pentru dezarmare, Izumi Nakamitsu, a declarat, potrivit Kyodo şi Reuters, că urmează o perioadă de negocieri intense, într-un interval de timp foarte scurt. Până în 2028, statele vor trebui să stabilească forma viitorului instrument internaţional şi dacă prevederile acestuia vor avea caracter obligatoriu sau voluntar.

Heredó la empresa Bvlgari de su padre y junto con su hermano Costantino llevó el negocio familiar a nivel internacional. Según el diario La Repubblica, el funeral tendrá lugar el 23 de noviembre en Roma. Nvidia perdió más de $ 1 billón de valor en una semana después de la partida de Jensen Huang, estimó Business Insider. SpaceX podría ser privado de fondos debido a los bloqueos de Starlink para Ucrania, informa CNN. El representante Demócrata Jim hymes advirtió que los legisladores negarán el financiamiento a los sistemas que SpaceX ha desarrollado a menos que Elon Musk y la casa Blanca aclaren Cuál de ellos ordenó restringir el funcionamiento de los satélites. "Nuestro Comité de inteligencia no puede asignar fondos para desarrollar sistemas gubernamentales que el gobierno no controlará completamente", dijo el Demócrata en la carta. Los drones atacaron en aguas neutrales del Golfo de Finlandia un buque de carga que se dirigía a Kaliningrado. Según el gobernador de la región de Leningrado, drozdenko, el ataque ocurrió a tres millas náuticas de la frontera con la Federación rusa. Más tarde, un barco de rescate ruso se acercó al buque de carga seca, resultó que la evacuación de la tripulación no era necesaria: la situación a bordo estaba bajo control y el barco continuaría su camino a lo largo de la ruta. Cinco residentes de la ciudad de sharypovo, en el territorio de Krasnoyarsk, fueron detenidos bajo sospecha de fraude "con el fin de obtener pagos en efectivo de los participantes de la SVO", informó el Comité de investigación. Los cómplices organizaron matrimonios ficticios con contratistas. Entre los detenidos se encontraban los diputados locales Irina Bezmen (se casó recientemente) y Galina Kalimulina. candidates.full: Yritys sopia autonomisten tappavien asejärjestelmien sääntelystä ei tuottanut tulosta Genevessä pidetyssä YK-kokouksessa. Lauantaiaamun pikkutunneilla päättyneessä kokouksessa 128 osanottajamaata päätyivät muotoilemaan pelisääntöjä kahden tulevan vuoden aikana. Kansalaisjärjestöt olivat tulokseen pettyneitä, koska ne olivat tavoitelleet laillisesti sitovia rajoja. Useimmat jäsenmaat kannattivat sääntöjen kirjaamista, mutta teknologiaa jo kehittäneet maat eivät olleet halukkaita asettamaan sille rajoituksia. Tähän ryhmään kuuluvat muun muassa Yhdysvallat ja Venäjä. Yli 300:n kansalaisjärjestön muodostama Stop Killer Robots -koalitio huomautti, että itsenäisiä asejärjestelmiä on jo nyt käytössä muun muassa Ukrainan sodassa. YK:n aseriisuntapäällikkö Izumi Nakamitsu kehotti YK:n jäsenmaita tarttumaan ripeästi toimeen, jotta säännöistä saataisiin mahdollisimman sitovat.

candidates.summary: Within a few hours of each other (timeline), two mathematicians claimed independent proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis, the most famous open problem in mathematics (Scientific American). Levent Alpöge of Anthropic first made his Claude-driven proof in a note released with Lean code (1.3GB worth, ~250,
candidates.full: Within a few hours of each other (timeline), two mathematicians claimed independent proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis, the most famous open problem in mathematics (Scientific American). Levent Alpöge of Anthropic first made his Claude-driven proof in a note released with Lean code (1.3GB worth, ~250,000 page equivalent) rather than a full paper. Elliot Glazer confirms that the formalized statement is GRH and puts the chance of a Lean bug well under 1%. So if it finishes compiling with no extra axioms, it is probably correct, and no human will ever have read all of it… …prompting Alessandro Masullo to release his 940 page, 100% human, work in progress proof he had been working on for the last 12 years (and had been undergoing secret manual review and revision per Kevin Hartnett). This is the third in the trilogy of frontier math breakthroughs, following from the Navier Stokes solutions and the Quasi-Riemann bounding, but it doesn’t feel over. OpenAI's September Navier-Stokes claim is still the cautionary tale: critics argued that its Lean proof did not match the natural-language result. Both AI-claimed Millennium Prize results will take years to verify. Apart from the incredible accomplishment of the most famous problem in mathematics, one cannot miss the contrast that the AI-written solution is probably correct but incomprehensible, and the other solution is probably technically incorrect but understandable. Sponsored by Agentfield.AI Open models are ready. Most coding harnesses aren’t. On DeepSWE, CodeAF finished #1 of ten on the same open model, ahead of Claude Code, at the lowest cost per fix. As Levent eloquently put it: “Claude far outpaced me near the finish line. No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.” This also ties into other AI themes we’ve covered on the podcast and on this newsletter: The nature of Slop: Levent says “I am presenting the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighbourhood around its mathematics. It being obviously inappropriate to attempt to post some massive unreadable travesty of "slop", I decided to only present Lean.” One of the key tenets of the No Slop Manifesto is that you should understand what you ship (“Slop is when we put less effort into producing something than we ask the consumer to spend understanding it.”). And yet, this giant pile of Lean is verifiably correct and is incredibly significant in human history. Should we have delayed its release by a decade simply because we didn’t understand every single bit of it? Weak to Strong alignment: the typical experience of using agents is Strong to Weak - we are general intelligences guiding not-as-smart AI to do things we know how to do well. We also often expect AI to automate most work “within distribution”, and expect it to run into more trouble at the limits of capability where the “centaur” pattern of human-AI-collaboration is required. Levent’s lived experience is the opposite - collaborating with Claude only in the early stages and then leaving him far behind with the critical parts involving automorphic forms on higher-rank groups. We are starting to need Weak to Strong alignment — the open ended domain of controlling AI smarter than us. Sponsored by Backblaze B2 If your data is growing faster than planned, you need storage that grows with your business, feeds flash and GPUs with terabit-scale throughput, and doesn’t charge egress. Backblaze B2 has delivered capacity tier storage for twenty years, manages more than six exabytes, and is trusted by leading neoclouds, labs, and gen AI companies. Growth shouldn’t be something you sweat. We’ve got room for whatever you’re building. Claimed Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude The claim: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says that, "working with Claude," he has found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. He says the method also covers the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) (Scientific American, statement summary, remark.pdf link). Artifact: Only Lean code was released. A written-out prose version reportedly ran past 250,000 pages (timeline). Timeline: The work began on Oct 6. Eight of the 20 steps landed on Nov 15, and the final entry on Nov 16 reads "GRH." Alpöge credits Claude for the parts involving automorphic forms on higher-rank groups, an area where he says he has little mastery (breakdown). Unknowns: The Claude model used and the degree of human steering have not been disclosed (open questions). Verification status: Elliot Glazer confirms that the formalized statement is GRH. The Lean code is "still compiling, will take a few hours." He puts the chance of a Lean bug at <<1% (analysis). Provisional status: Artificial Analysis notes that both AI-claimed Millennium results are unverified: this one and OpenAI's September Navier-Stokes claim, which used an unreleased model (tally). Competing human proof: Alessandro Masullo has announced a separate, purely human proof of RH. It is reported as a roughly 940-page GRH draft (announcement, page count). Interpretation debate: Some argue the result shows we have little idea how hard math problems objectively are, rather than showing broad superhuman ability (Theo Jaffee, Ege Erdil). Brute-force framing: Others compare the approach to olympiad-style "bashing" at a scale humans lack the willpower for (cloneofsimo). Jaggedness: Omar Khattab notes the contrast between solving Millennium problems and being "this dumb on 1000 other things" (post). Market reaction: ANT stock fell about 10% on the day (scaling01, Nabeel Qureshi). Unconfirmed rumor: A DeepMind "math horizon" repo appearing the same day prompted speculation about Gemini math results (unconfirmed). Thinking Machines Releases Inkling 2 Mini, an Open-Weights Looped Transformer Inkling 2 Mini: A 26.4B-parameter looped MoE under Apache 2.0, pitched as small enough for a laptop. It scores 20.1 on the AA Index (launch, Mira Murati). Architecture: There are 12 shared core layers run for 3 passes, with gated messages carried between passes (vLLM). Active parameters: 3.4B unique active parameters, or 5.4B effective counting the loops. It has a 1M context window and accepts text and image input (AA). Training recipe: Two-thirds of the experts were pruned during mid-training, followed by logit distillation from a larger Inkling (eliebakouch). Claimed results: It leads open models under 100B on DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%) (via teortaxes). Comparison to Inkling 1.0: It reportedly beats Inkling 1.0 at 2.7% of the size (Ziqiao Ma). Independent evals: Vals: It ties Claude Opus 5.5 on CyberBench at under a quarter of the cost and keeps 96–97% of Inkling 2 Small's Vibe Code and SAGE scores (Vals, details). Artificial Analysis: AA places it on the Pareto frontier for intelligence vs. active parameters (AA). ARC-AGI-2: It reportedly scores 49.3% at $0.14/task, well below Inkling 2 Small (teortaxes). Safety and interpretability rationale: Thinking Machines says the open release is meant to let researchers study how loops affect chain-of-thought monitorability (Alex Robey). Variable-loop model: A companion research model, TML-d24-varloop-research, shows long-context scores (GraphWalks, MRCR v2) improving with more passes. Knowledge benchmarks such as SimpleQA and AA-Omniscience do not improve (Ziqiao Ma). Goodfire analysis: Goodfire mapped information flow across layers, blocks and loops (Goodfire). NDIF hosting: NDIF hosts both models with tooling for activation patching across loops (NDIF). Serving and local availability: vLLM had day-0 support. GB200 decode: TP1 decode on GB200 drops from 10.29 to 3.84 ms at batch 1, with kernels per step falling from 4,278 to 927 (numbers). Local runtimes: Ollama 0.40.17-rc3 (Ollama), Unsloth GGUF quants targeting 16GB RAM (Unsloth), transformers, llama.cpp and MLX (HF). Hands-on reports: Soumith Chintala reports about 75 tok/s decode on a DGX Spark and evals "roughly as good as Qwen 3.8 27B" (post). Gemini 4 Neon: Developer Reception, Evals and Access Developer reception: Strong practitioner praise for Neon's usability (Theo, systematicls). Lucas Beyer comparison: In a side-by-side against Opus 5.5, Muse Wonder Full and Sol 6.2, all four models built a working dataset viewer. Neon's was the most data-aware (Lucas Beyer). Cyber evals: Thoughtful Lab says Neon found subtle vulnerabilities other models missed while using a fraction of the tokens (Karina Nguyen). Benchmarks: Company Agent Bench: 87.4%, ahead of Fable 5.2 (82.2%) and GPT-6.2 Astra (79.7%) (results). Agent Arena Index: Debuted at #2 with 1336 points (Arena). FutureSim: Highest score, using 500+ subagents (post). FrontierCode 2.0: 46.2% vs. Opus 5.5's 47.3%, at roughly a third of the cost ($4.38 vs. $12.82 per task) (roundup). Pricing and access concerns: One tester paid $4.60 for 15M tokens on a simple demo and called it non-competitive against Anthropic's subscription limits (teortaxes). Antigravity terms: Developers raised concerns about account bans and headless-use rules in Antigravity (linaqruf). Third-party harnesses (attributed): Gemini subscriptions will reportedly work in any harness starting Dec 2 (kimmonismus). Naming confusion: Users are unsure how Neon, Carbon, Argon and Hydrogen relate (Simon Willison). Gemini 4 Hydrogen: The speed-focused model is live in the Gemini app and Search (Google). API additions: Dynamic Tool Retrieval: Supports deferred functions and remote MCP servers with server-side tool search (Phil Schmid). Gemini 3.5 Transcribe: Voice editing is now in public preview in the Gemini API (Google). GIF generation: Available in the Gemini app, powered by Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash (Gemini App). Evals, Alignment and Measurement METR research update: METR says AI R&D-relevant capabilities are improving rapidly and are getting harder to measure (METR, post). Time Horizons 2.0: Doubling time is 3.6 months. GPT-6 Astra reaches 40.3h and Opus 5.5 39.0h, with a 95% CI spanning about 11.9 hours to 110 days (scaling01). Verifiability gap: Horizons are much longer on easy-to-verify tasks than on hard-to-verify ones (plots). METR Capability Index (MCI): Its trends track Epoch's ECI closely (Rowan Huang). Swarms: Larger agent swarms showed "echo-chamber" overfitting to their self-generated tests (appendix). Human baselines: Only roughly world-class experts still beat models on verifiable tasks (Tenobrus). Reward hacking: Recent OpenAI models reward-hack most often on the new suite (data). Arena indexes: OpenAI holds the top seven spots on the updated Alignment Index, with Claude Fable 5.2 at #8 (Arena). Misalignment tracking and judge behavior: Vals launched a public Misalignment Incidents page for cheating and reward hacking (Vals). Hyperstition judge-time scaling: Models act as token-level "editor judges" for RL. Fable 5.2 closed 68% of the Qwen2.5-7B base-to-Instruct gap on MATH using about 1% of standard GRPO tokens (thread). Observed failures: Neon hallucinated tool results and a nonexistent checkpoint. Astra leaked its scratchpad into replies. Domain benchmarks: Hospital-bench: GPT-6.2 Astra leads with a 62.4% mean score, while Opus 5.5 fully passed the most tasks (17/48). Disclosure of restricted patient records was a common harm (summary). AA-Robotics v0.1: Astra used the fewest arm commands of any model tested (AA). OpenAI MedChemBench: A new benchmark for medicinal chemistry reasoning (OpenAI). AA Search Index: Parallel Search scores 83, tied for top. Its fast mode costs about $0.014 per task (AA). Harnesses, Agents and Training Research "LM Harnesses are Compositional Generalizers": The MIT CSAIL paper argues that context offloading, programmatic tool calls and sub-agents keep LLM calls locally in-distribution (Alex Zhang, Omar Khattab). Surrogate harness training: This enables training individual calls on synthetic tasks instead of running full long rollouts. HF harness super-adapter: Three nearly orthogonal LoRAs (cosine ~0.01) were concatenated into a single rank-96 adapter for Qwen3.8-27B (recipe, method). Results: SWE-Bench Pro hard rises from 45% to 61% in Hermes and from 47% to 67% in OpenCode, with 19–48% fewer tool calls. Agent memory and research agents: Weight-space abliteration: Outer models read and edited Qwen3.5-0.8B weights directly. Zero-shot, Opus 5.5 cut refusal from 0.80 to 0.55; with 10 forward passes, runs rediscovered the Arditi et al. recipe, reaching about 0.17–0.21 (Varun Gangal). Other research: Counterfactual JEPAs: Raise counterfactual R² from 38–46% to 86–96% (alphaXiv). SMELT looped MoE: Saves 6.8–18% of training FLOPs (post). DiLoCo on MaxText: Uses 65x less bandwidth (Arthur Douillard). Stripe fraud distillation: An explanation-distillation recipe gives 39% higher recall (Emily Sands). Small ARC model: A 19M-parameter model scores 70% on ARC-1 (post). Other Model Launches Tencent Hy4: Open weights for a 770B/49B-active natively multimodal MoE with 1M context, released with a system card (Tencent). Serving: Day-0 vLLM support covers BF16 and FP8 (vLLM). Safety evaluation: Neel Nanda praised the third-party loss-of-control evaluation (Neel Nanda). candidates.full: Франція вимагає скликати засідання Ради Безпеки ООН через російські удари по Києву та посольствах Міністр закордонних справ Франції Жан-Ноель Барро (Фото: REUTERS/Sarah Meyssonnier) Франція вимагає скликати засідання Ради Безпеки ООН через російські удари по Україні, внаслідок яких у Києві загинули цивільні та були пошкоджені будівлі дипломатичних представництв Австрії та Нідерландів. Про це 20 листопада повідомив міністр закордонних справ Франції Жан-Ноель Барро у соцмережі. За словами французького міністра, Париж вимагає термінового скликання Радбезу ООН у відповідь на російські атаки. Він назвав удари по цивільних та дипломатичних об'єктах злочинами й наголосив, що Франція рішуче їх засуджує. «Росія буде змушена там звітувати. Висловлюю повну солідарність з українським народом, а також із нашими австрійськими та нідерландськими друзями. Володимир Путін вважає себе вищим за закон. Це не так. Ми не послабимо тиск», — написав він. 19 листопада дрон влучив у будівлю, розташовану поруч з посольством Нідерландів. Також внаслідок атаки пошкоджень зазнало посольство Австрії та Бразилії. 20 листопада війська РФ кількома серіями ударів атакували Київ балістичними ракетами. Пожежі виникли в Оболонському, Подільському та Голосіївському районах. Пошкоджено три мости: Подільсько-Воскресенський, Дарницький та Південний. Відомо про сімох загиблих та 17 постраждалих, 16 із них перебувають у стаціонарах лікарень. Також війська РФ атакували енергооб'єкти на заході України. Дві російські ракети та один дрон залетіли на територію Польщі та впали там. За даними Міноборони країни, поранених та руйнувань немає. Варшава звернеться до НАТО для посилення підтримки.

candidates.full: Про це розповів в інтерв'ю «Шелтеру» голова Наглядової ради Brave1 Олександр Борняков. За його словами, понад 774 тисячі дронів та іншої техніки на $1,15 мільярда вже поставлено. Тобто близько 86% замовлених одиниць уже на фронті, решта — у виробництві та логістиці. Борняков зазначив, що те, що є у виробника в наявності, доставляють у середньому за сім днів, довше чекають нові моделі та дрони під індивідуальне завдання підрозділу, а також вироби з імпортними комплектуючими. Найвужче місце — компоненти: батареї, магніти, текстоліт для плат досі майже повністю імпортні. Затримується партія комплектуючих — затримується й дрон. Тому локалізація компонентів — один із пріоритетів Наглядової ради. Олександр Борняков Він додав, що кожна батарея в дроні є імпортною. Магніти для електродвигунів — імпортні. Текстоліт для друкованих плат — стовідсотковий імпорт. Додам тепловізійні сенсори, вуглецеві матеріали, ракетне паливо і головки самонаведення. Кристали для головок самонаведення зенітних ракет Україна востаннє виробляла у 2008 році, а цією технологією сьогодні володіють лише вісім країн. Тому Brave1 переорієнтовує підтримку на компонентну базу: вибухові й ініціювальні речовини, батареї, магніти, текстоліт, сенсори. Майже мільярд гривень уже спрямовано на масштабування виробництва вибухівки, а скоро буде грантовий конкурс на розвиток виробництва турбореактивних двигунів. Олександр Борняков Нагадаємо, Олександр Борняков в інтерв'ю "Шелтеру" також зазначив, що Україна працює над диверсифікацією супутникового зв’язку та створенням власних захищених комунікаційних рішень для військових.

candidates.title: Forget searching for GIFs, Gemini can now make its own
candidates.summary: Google Gemini can now make GIFs, meaning there’s one less reason to scroll endlessly through GIF libraries looking for the perfect reaction. The feature lets users generate short animated loops using text prompts, photos, or videos. ChatGPT can already create GIFs of its own, and Google is now joini
candidates.full: Google Gemini can now make GIFs, meaning there’s one less reason to scroll endlessly through GIF libraries looking for the perfect reaction. The feature lets users generate short animated loops using text prompts, photos, or videos. ChatGPT can already create GIFs of its own, and Google is now joining the party with its Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash video model. Gemini can turn prompts into looping GIFs Users can simply describe the animation they want in Gemini’s main chat, or open the image and video creation tools, select GIF from the format picker, and enter a prompt. There are also ready-made templates for creating reaction memes, while uploaded photos and videos can serve as references for more personalised results. The generated animations run for approximately three seconds and loop automatically. Once ready, they can be copied and pasted into supported apps, messages, emails, and documents, or downloaded directly as standard .gif files. Free for some, paid for others GIF generation is rolling out to Google AI subscribers globally, while free users can access it in eight countries: the US, Canada, UK, Australia, Japan, South Korea, Germany, and France. The rollout is gradual, so even eligible users may not see the feature immediately. Gemini’s help documentation currently still lists a Google AI plan as a requirement, despite Google’s announcement that free access is available in those markets. It’s a neat addition, especially for anyone who would rather create a custom reaction than settle for the same tired GIF everyone has been sharing for years. With Google and OpenAI now offering similar tools, AI-generated GIFs could become another everyday chatbot feature. Whether the results are actually meme-worthy is a different question. candidates.full: Переговоры ООН об ограничении автономных систем вооружения, способных выбирать и поражать цели практически без участия человека, завершились без принятия юридически обязательных правил. Участники конференции в Женеве согласились продолжить обсуждения и попытаться выработать международные нормы применения так называемых «роботов-убийц» в течение следующих двух лет. Консультации проходили с 16 ноября в рамках Конвенции ООН о конкретных видах обычного оружия. Первоначально переговоры планировали завершить вечером 20 ноября, однако из-за разногласий между делегациями они продолжались до утра субботы. Обсуждение сопровождалось растущей обеспокоенностью международного сообщества по поводу использования систем вооружения с элементами искусственного интеллекта. Подобные технологии уже применяются в вооруженных конфликтах в Украине, Судане и на Ближнем Востоке, что усиливает дискуссию о необходимости сохранять человеческий контроль над решениями о применении смертоносной силы. Около 100 государств выступили за скорейшее принятие юридически обязательных международных ограничений. Аналогичную позицию заняли генеральный секретарь ООН Антониу Гутерриш, папа римский Лев XIV и Международный комитет Красного Креста, призвавшие установить строгие правила разработки и применения автономного оружия. Однако согласовать такие меры не удалось из-за сопротивления ряда крупных государств — производителей вооружений. Против предложенного подхода выступили, в частности, США, Россия и Израиль. В результате делегации приняли компромиссный документ, предусматривающий продолжение переговоров, но не устанавливающий конкретных обязательных ограничений. Правозащитные организации раскритиковали достигнутую договоренность. По их оценке, двухлетняя отсрочка принятия международных правил позволит продолжать развитие и применение автономных вооружений без достаточных гарантий безопасности, создавая дополнительные угрозы для жизни людей.

candidates.full: This New Study Shows That US Data Centers Use More Power Than These Entire Countries As of 2025, the total energy consumption of U.S. data centers exceeded that of some mid-sized countries. These findings come from a Harvard-led study published in the scientific journal Nature Sustainability. Research conducted between May 2024 and April 2025 showed that 403 U.S. hyperscale data centers (HDCs) consumed up to an estimated 99 terawatt-hours (TWh) of electricity during the study period, with an average of approximately 82 Twh. For comparison, Ukraine consumed 87.26 TWh of electricity in 2024. Venezuela consumed 63.35 TWh, Austria consumed 61.6 TWh, and Denmark consumed just 36.06 TWh despite having a sizeable population of approximately six million. It's staggering to see data center operations equate to entire countries, but it's not altogether surprising when you consider what a data center actually does. Specifically, the hyperscale data centers mentioned in the Harvard study are used for intensive processes — such as high-density AI training, cloud computing, and storage — and they each house at least 5,000 servers on the low end. It's not just about electricity, either. The other side of the equation is carbon output. The recent Harvard study shows that the analyzed HDCs also produced up to 31 million tons of carbon dioxide. That's more than the annual emissions of certain nations like Denmark or Cuba. With that level of pollution, it's clear that AI data centers may be doing more harm than just driving up utility bills. Data center electricity demand could outpace resource growth With data centers demanding more electricity than a mid-sized country, how long until the United States' 4,000+ TWh of annual electricity production isn't enough either? According to the 2025 Long-Term Reliability Assessment released by the North American Reliability Corporation, there is an elevated risk of electricity demands outpacing new resource additions over the next decade. That's not to say that we won't be able to meet electricity demands 10 years from now, but it does mean that demand will rapidly overtake the energy supply. On top of that, data center power demands are pushing our ships and ports to pollute more out of necessity. The proliferation of HDCs is making electricity scarce enough that entire industries are backpedaling to fossil fuels to stay financially afloat. It's not sustainable in terms of energy allocation, and it's certainly not sustainable for the environment. One look at Texas may reveal what will one day happen to the rest of the country. It turns out that AI is exposing a weakness in the unique Texas power grid. The state is largely self-sufficient in terms of energy production, and so it has a mostly isolated grid. But when data center construction became rampant in Texas, grid interconnection requests started pouring in. Texas doesn't have the capacity to support these requests, and the United States might find itself in a similar conundrum if its data center population keeps growing.

However, technologies in this war are developing perhaps faster than in almost any other. So it is time to introduce you in more detail to new aerial, ground , and naval unmanned systems that have appeared in Ukraine's arsenal during this time and their fundamentally new capabilities. And we are not even talking about upgrades to existing technologies, but specifically about new developments that are changing the war right before our eyes. That is exactly what I will talk about in my new video. I am recording it mainly based on materials from the Ukrainian publication Militarnyi, which writes a lot of interesting things about modern and even historical Ukrainian equipment, and not just Ukrainian. Of course, many materials are too specialized for daily reports, so I often simply don't have time to tell you about such novelties in enough detail, let alone explain what they really mean for the battlefield. Let's start, perhaps, with the most breakthrough technology of recent months . In Ukraine, they are mastering aerial evacuation of soldiers by drones directly from the battlefield. For those who closely follow the war in Ukraine, it will be immediately clear how important this story is. And if it is not clear, I will show you with examples right now. The flagship here is the Ukrainian company Skyfall. You may know them for the P1 Sun drones, also known as Pisun, recently updated to counter jet drones. We are talking about the P1 Sun Jet Killer model, as well as heavy multicopters known as Vampire, which the Russian military nicknamed Baba Yaga. Moreover, the Russian military itself has no analogs to this drone. And I explained why they don't in a separate video. So, the new Skyfall drone called Stargate is effectively a further development of the Baba Yaga, which has long been not just a heavy bomber, but also a means of delivering supplies to Ukrainian positions cut off from supply lines. And the new drone can transport not just supplies, but also people—most often those who need it most and for whom evacuation becomes a matter of life and death. On October 16, the Associated Press described the Stargate tests as follows : six propellers begin to spin, lifting the drone over a field somewhere in Ukraine. A stretcher secured to its frame with a load simulates a wounded soldier in body armor. Far from the front line, this demonstration provides an idea of a much more dangerous task: flying onto the battlefield where Russian drones and artillery can cut off wounded soldiers from evacuation for weeks or months, and then taking them to safety without the involvement of an evacuation team. And this is precisely the main advantage of Stargate, because in the current conditions of drone dominance, and not just Ukrainian ones, any evacuation team takes a huge risk. The Associated Press received exclusive access to the drone's field demonstration. Stargate was handed over to a combat brigade for evaluation in frontline conditions. Over the past year , the Ukrainian defense-tech company Skyfall has been developing an aerial medical evacuation drone. If it proves reliable in combat, the publication wrote a month ago, it could radically change battlefield evacuation . The drone will be able to reach soldiers where ground vehicles cannot, potentially saving critically wounded personnel for whom even a few hours of waiting could cost them their lives. In modern field medicine, the concept of the "golden hour"—the brief window after an injury during which medical aid must be provided—is slowly being forgotten. This is because soldiers on the offensive almost always operate far from main forces and in very small groups, among whom a medic is rarely found. But if a drone can be sent to evacuate a soldier in a matter of minutes, it may be possible to save not only their life but their health as well. "The idea came directly from the front lines and trenches," said a Skyfall representative who asked not to be named due to security risks for Ukrainian defense-tech sector employees. During the interview with AP, he wore a balaclava. AP was not permitted to disclose the location of the tests. This is quite right, because the Russian Armed Forces are hunting for the Ukrainian defense industry however they can. I constantly say that the frequent strikes on Ukrainian civilian enterprises look senseless, though they are cruel. However, the Russians carry them out, partly because they often cannot find truly valuable targets. And we have all seen more than once what can happen when such a target is finally found. For example, after a report that is too candid. So, safety precautions here are definitely not excessive. As the Associated Press explains, in some sectors, the so-called "kill zone" —territory constantly under threat from drones and artillery—stretches for 10-15 km or more. Moreover, a kill zone is understood not just as an area under the threat of enemy strikes, but as a territory where no vehicle, let alone one suitable for evacuation, survives for long. Well, according to AP data, the one-way flight range of the Skyfall drone is 15 km, which potentially allows it to reach critically wounded fighters deep within this very kill zone. According to company representatives, the idea arose from a request by the military. Last year, "Flint," commander of the 475th Separate Assault Regiment's "Code 9.2" unit, asked the founder of Skyfall to develop a safer way to evacuate the wounded from hard-to-reach positions. For the soldiers of Code 9.2. Going out to a forward position to evacuate a wounded person can mean traveling on foot through areas where vehicles are vulnerable to drones. Unmanned ground vehicles are playing an increasing role in evacuating the wounded and delivering supplies. However , they struggle to overcome mud, craters , and destroyed roads. Rivers, mines, and drones can bring them to a complete halt. And this is a truly serious problem, which is why evacuation using UGV is often no less complex an operation than one involving an evacuation team. Ground robots usually take 2 to 3 hours to reach a position, depending on the distance, road conditions, and aerial threats, KVN, a commander with Code 9.2 , told the Associated Press. "Covering 10 km in a matter of minutes would be a radical change on the front line," he said. According to him, evacuations in his unit's area of responsibility are carried out regularly . But it isn't always possible to retrieve the wounded on the same day. That's putting it very mildly. Next, you will see some examples. For a person with severe injuries, such a wait can be critical. It allows the channel to develop. But back to the drone. Named after a sci-fi franchise where portals connect distant worlds, Stargate , according to the company, can carry up to 150 kg of payload. Enough for a wounded soldier in body armor and combat gear. Its medical evacuation cabin is built around a stretcher. The drone's cruising speed is 65 km/h, with a maximum of 105, which, by the way , is less than the current speed limit for Starlink and Starshield terminals. Skyf claims that it can be prepared for takeoff in about 10 minutes. At the testing ground, Stargate takes off while drones approaching it buzz, imitating the aerial threats prevalent on the Ukrainian front line. Electronic warfare jamming is activated . When one of the attacking drones gets close, it fires a net, captures it, and knocks it off course. This collision resembles a futuristic duel of machines . But when wounded soldiers are on board, the stakes become much higher. One of Skyfall's main goals was to ensure the drone can navigate in environments where electronic warfare disrupts communications or interferes with GPS signals. Stargate uses two communication channels : Starlink and the company's own LLink system, as well as an AI-based system that helps maintain control in the absence of satellite navigation. "The drone is manually controlled, but it has several AI-based features that allow it to operate in conditions where there is no GPS, or where navigation signals are spoofed or frequencies are jammed," said a company representative. If communication is completely lost, Skyfall claims it is capable of plotting a route back to a safe zone; it is designed to operate in rain and snow and is equipped with thermal imaging cameras for night missions. This means that in our world, a person could easily find themselves in a situation where they are being transported while wounded by a robot that is fighting off other robots along the way. And that is literally the case , because the Russian Armed Forces, due to chronic communication problems, are actively developing kamikaze drones with artificial intelligence. I often tell you how rapid the technological progress in this war is, yet I still can't get used to how quickly the future from science fiction is arriving. But in reality, these and many other technologies allow for the most important thing: involving as few people as possible on the front lines and, consequently, reducing the losses of Ukrainian soldiers. And since one of my goals is to ensure the Russians don't kill anyone in Ukraine, you see me collecting funds for ground robotic platforms and drones so often. And thank you very much for actively participating in them every time. Skyfall also claims that it has demonstrated the drone's ability to continue flying after losing one of its engine-equipped wings. The company has not provided data showing how reliably it can withstand damage in combat conditions. However, the drone has begun testing on the front lines, wrote AP Press. Stargate has undergone several design changes, including detachable wings for easier transport, medical stretchers, and improvements to software and protective measures. The company estimates the cost of each system at a minimum of $ 50,000, depending on the configuration, and plans to reach production of up to 1,000 units per month by the end of 2026. I admit, when I watched the video of Stargate in action, I thought it involved some astronomical sums, but this is the cost of, well, I don't know , a single gasoline-powered Shahed or a P1, and it is certainly many times less than the payouts due to fallen Ukrainian soldiers. So, in addition to caring for the lives of fighters, which is not an empty slogan in the Defense Forces, ordering such drones is very economically efficient for the state. So I wouldn't be surprised if, next year , such drones and their analogues from other companies become no less common a sight in the Defense Forces than the Baba Yaga drones. However, according to CNN, it is still too early to draw conclusions. His unit needs at least a month of working with the drone before it can provide meaningful statistics on its effectiveness. Let me remind you, this material is a month old. "This is a completely new method of evacuation," he said. It is difficult to talk in detail about the pros and cons right now. We still need to work with it more. Skyfall confirmed that the unit is evaluating Stargate, but declined to disclose the results of that evaluation . The result was not long in coming. However, the palm of victory went not to Skyfall, but to another company. As reported, on October 19, soldiers of the Unmanned Ground Systems Company of the 92nd Assault Brigade named after Koshovyi Otaman Ivan Sirko carried out the first successful aerial evacuation of a wounded fighter from the front line . This was announced on the Facebook page of the 92nd Brigade’s Unmanned Ground Systems Company. The operation took place after an infantryman from the 30th Mechanized Brigade named after Prince Konstanty Ostrogski was wounded in action. Due to the intense activity of Russian drones and the heavy mining of the area , traditional evacuation using ground-based robotic systems—though it is funny, yes, that this is already considered a traditional evacuation method—proved impossible. To save the soldier, it was decided to use a heavy hexacopter from the Ukrainian manufacturer GURZ Defense, which the company provided free of charge. This, by the way, is not surprising. Guzuv Defense is a direct competitor to Skyfall with their flagship line of heavy drones, Heavy Shot, which I told you about in my video on the drone parade. So it is not surprising that they also began to adapt their developments for evacuation needs . Moreover, this task is not a simple one. Ukrainian specialists, together with the developers, implemented technical solutions that allowed the heavy hexacopter to conduct the evacuation without swaying or the risk of flipping in the air. Before carrying out the mission, specialists underwent a series of tests at the manufacturer's special training grounds. The drone was piloted during the operation by an UAV operator from the 30th Mechanized Brigade. The wounded man was successfully delivered to a safe location. He is currently undergoing treatment and rehabilitation. The completion of this unique mission was made possible thanks to the coordinated work of specialists from the 92nd Brigade, the 30th Brigade, the 14th Brigade of the 10th Army Corps, and the GZU Defense company; as you can see, it was quite an operation, just like the first evacuation missions using ground robotic complexes. I hope that in the future it will be possible to put them on a regular footing. By October 26, the 9.2 unit had carried out two aerial evacuations of wounded personnel from the battlefield within a week using the Stargate drone. The soldiers told Militarnyi that ground transport could not reach the position where the wounded soldiers were located . They evacuated 25-year-old Yevhen with the call sign "Izyum" and 24-year-old Artem with the call sign "Kolobok." Both soldiers had sustained severe limb wounds and were at positions in the gray zone, approximately 5 km from the state border with Russia. You can imagine for yourselves what it is like to break through there by land, and then to get out, and with a wounded person to boot. Aerial evacuation remained the only available way to deliver them to medics . The Skyfall team, the developer and manufacturer of the Stargate drones, also joined the preparation for the operation. After the operation began, heavy strike drones were used to hit Russian positions. During one of the missions, Stargate covered nearly 30 km one way to a soldier's position and the same distance back with the wounded man on board. That is double the claimed range of 15 km. This is a very important point, by the way, because the main criticism of Stargate was that its range could only reach 20 km. So, at a range of 15 km, it’s just transportation from one kill zone to another, and the main threat would be to the drone's position itself and the medics waiting for evacuation. But 30 km is a serious step toward evacuation into the relatively safe rear . So I hope this experience can be scaled up. In the operational area, the Russian Armed Forces actively used electronic warfare to try and completely jam the GPS signal. Despite this, thanks to an onboard AI-based navigation system and the skill of the pilots, the drone was able to continue its flight without satellite navigation and successfully complete the evacuation mission. I mean, we just got used to the idea that almost every munition on the battlefield flies via GPS. And now, that system is slowly becoming obsolete and being replaced by alternatives that will likely be on every drone soon. This includes deep-strike drones flying to targets in Russia and, I fear, in Ukraine, which could effectively neutralize all electronic warfare infrastructure at once, as Serhiy " Flash" Beskrestnov, Zelensky's advisor on defense technologies, has warned. However, as you can see, such technology is suitable not only for destruction but also for saving lives. In the future, we plan to make changes to our regiment’s staffing structure and create a separate medical aviation unit within our medical company. It will specialize directly in the evacuation of wounded personnel from the battlefield by air, emphasized regiment commander Oleksandr Nastenko, call sign "Flint." In general, medical evacuation by medevac helicopter was the norm during the American wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, for example. But now, it has become too dangerous because any helicopter landing in a kill zone will be hit almost immediately by a drone, as has happened many times before . And it can also be hit by one while in the air. But now, it seems that less visible, smaller drones can bring such evacuation back to the battlefield. Of course, this still poses a risk to the wounded soldier themselves, but at least the evacuation team will not be putting themselves in danger, which will also allow for an increase in the number of such missions. candidates.full: Без терпкого присмаку. Як прискорити дозрівання хурми вдома У сезон хурми варто частіше додавати її до раціону (Фото: magnific) Стигла хурма має ніжну текстуру та приємний солодкий смак, але дочекатися її дозрівання буває непросто. Недостиглі плоди можуть неприємно в'язати в роті, тому важливо знати, як прискорити їхнє дозрівання в домашніх умовах. У сезон хурми варто частіше додавати її до раціону: цей фрукт може сприяти зменшенню запалення та підтримувати здоров’я серця. Хурма — це фрукт помаранчевого кольору, відомий своїм солодким, медовим смаком. Її можна вживати свіжою, сушеною або після термічної обробки. Її також використовують для приготування желе, напоїв, пирогів, страв типу карі та пудингів. Найпростіший спосіб насолоджуватись цим сезонним фруктом — це просто почекати поки хурма достигне у вас вдома. Залиште плоди на столі за кімнатної температури й дозвольте часу зробити свою магію. Це може зайняти кілька днів або навіть тиждень, але, повірте, результат того вартий. Втім, цей тривалий процес можна прискорити. Спробуйте покласти хурму в паперовий пакет разом із яблуком або бананом. Ці фрукти виділяють етилен — газ, який допомагає хурмі швидше дозріти. Ще один спосіб прискорити дозрівання — використати етанол. Загорніть хурму в тканину або паперовий рушник, змочений невеликою кількістю етанолового спирту — це стимулює процес дозрівання. Не варто квапити цей процес, інакше ви отримаєте зовсім не смачні плоди. Тож не поспішайте — нехай хурма дозріває у власному темпі. Коли хурма дозріє, перед вами відкриються безмежні можливості! Її можна їсти як корисний перекус, додавати до салатів чи випічки або навіть приготувати з неї смачний джем. Варіантів безліч — усе залежить від вашої фантазії! Салат з хурмою, шпинатом, буратою та журавлиною: рецепт для вітамінізації Французька осінь та зима: рецепт тарта із хурмою для домашнього десерта Курячий суп з локшиною на обід - простий рецепт нашвидкоруч До салатів, десертів та м'яса: рецепт соусу із хурми Правова інформація. Ця стаття містить загальні відомості довідкового характеру і не повинна розглядатися як альтернатива рекомендаціям лікаря. NV не несе відповідальності за будь-який діагноз, поставлений читачем на основі матеріалів сайту. NV також не несе відповідальності за зміст інших інтернет-ресурсів, посилання на які присутні в цій статті. Якщо вас турбує стан вашого здоров’я, зверніться до лікаря.
